Area.evidence_source: Statements such as 'I had decided to die' could illustrate the interviewees' determination prior to the suicide attempt. Other statements, such as: 'If I had had more pills I would have taken more' and 'If I had had weapons available that night a month ago, I wouldn't have been alive today', seem to be expressions of a strong desire and willingness to die. The reflection: 'Did I have luck or bad luck?' seems to illustrate that the interviewees do not immediately feel joy of having survived. To many, it seems like a coincidence that they were found or managed to report the overdose in time, either to a friend or to the emergency ward, while one interviewee says: 'I really just wanted to get help'. Some of the interviewees were frightened by their own actions, especially by 'the courage part'. Two male interviewees said, however, that now they felt more confident that they would be able to carry out an eventual suicide, and one of them said that his fear of death was less. A woman said: 'I think everything is easier if you've done it once, then you can do it several times. I hope not, but I'm afraid I can do it' (i.e. to accomplish a new suicide attempt). As I swallowed the sleeping pills down with red wine, I was thinking, ah, now it'll be over. Then the feeling came, that you get a little happy, because you know somehow that now the race is run, now you're finished... And then, when I woke up next morning and realized that I had not made it I got really pissed off... But then I realized that I had taken too little, so I stumbled back home, and then I took something I had left in another box... I thought that now it's certainly over, and then the same feeling came again, when I realized that it started to work, it was such a relief to know that now at least you should make it. Then I woke up, as my wife was standing there, shaking me violently, shaking life back into my body, I can remember being very annoyed. I considered very carefully, then I was beginning to be affected by the pills already, as I was lying in bed and had been chewing pills for several hours, and had counted all the pills I had and thought that I'll manage to make it with these. But then I remembered clearly from last time that, I woke up again 2 ½ years ago thinking: Oh, my God, if I fail again this time, it must not happen, if I decide to die, then I must die, somehow. But I was very determined that I should do it. I cried a lot while I was in my room and I wrote a farewell letter, this time as well (to my grown up children and other close relatives), just a short note. And there I was sitting in the evening, counting pills, with a bunch in each hand, shall – shall not, shall – shall not, but something held me back. The interviewees expressed some of the considerations preceding the suicide attempt. Responsibility for family members was especially emphasized as difficult. Also, responsibility for their own lives, to complete projects in life, such as a vocational training, had to be weighed against the desire to avoid suffering. One of the interviewees described the conflict involved in the suicide decision, as 'a clear spirit being present all the time, that I want to make it an end and at the same time I can see the value of living'. Suicide is not regarded as an easy decision and solution, but as an expression of a struggle between the desire for relief from suffering and a longing for life, where the suffering gets the upper hand.
